chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Saqr ibn Dolaf, on the authority of Yasir - the servant, that he had heard Abul Hassan Ali ibn Musa Al-Ridha (peace be upon him)
“Whoever draws a comparison between the Sublime God and His creatures is an atheist. Whoever ascribes to God what God has admonished against is also an atheist.”

key_terms.مُشْرِكٌ: One who associates partners with God (atheist/polytheist in this context)

ai.seo_question: What are the two main ways one commits shirk or kufr regarding God's attributes according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the boundaries of divine unity by identifying two specific errors: likening God to creation (tashbih) constitutes shirk, while attributing to Him what He has excluded from His nature constitutes kufr. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, underscores the Shia emphasis on precise theological articulation to distinguish between mere anthropomorphism and fundamental denial of divine perfection. It serves as a critical reference for understanding how deviations in attribute attribution lead to distinct categories of theological error.
